chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, through his chain, elevating it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family):
God the Exalted the Sublime said, 'O Children of Adam! Obey Me in what I order you to do, and do not teach Me what is best for you.'

key_terms.فِيمَا أَمَرْتُكَ: In what I have commanded you
key_terms.مَا يُصْلِحُكَ: What is best for you / what benefits you
key_terms.يَا ابْنَ آدَمَ: O Children of Adam (address to humanity)

ai.seo_question: What does God mean when He says 'do not teach Me what is best for you'?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith qudsi to highlight the fundamental posture of *ubudiyyah* (servitude), where humans obey divine commands without presuming to advise the Creator on their own welfare. This concept underscores the epistemological gap between the All-Knowing and the created, reinforcing that true benefit lies in submission to God's wisdom rather than human self-referential judgment. It serves as a spiritual corrective against arrogance, reminding believers that God's decrees are inherently beneficial even when their wisdom is not fully comprehended.
